subject: Operational split and evidence delivery for HIPAA pilot
messages:
From: Sara Khan <sara.khan@medistry.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonathan Park <jonathan.park@medistry.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: HIPAA package pricing — evidence delivery and amortization question

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the overview during yesterday's call. A couple follow-ups from procurement so we can finish our internal approval:

1) Can you confirm how Redwood proposes to amortize the HIPAA add-on (audit logs + KMS/HSM + residency)? Our finance team prefers a single implementation charge that can be capitalized rather than recurring per-seat fees.
2) For audit evidence (SOC-like artifacts, audit log extracts), what is the delivery cadence and format? Do you provide a checklist or package we can attach to our compliance binder?
3) If we commit to a 12-month Reserved capacity + HIPAA add-on, what discount tiers are available and how do you allocate credits between KMS seat fees vs. audit log retention costs?

We'd like a written sketch we can circulate to our CFO and security team. If helpful, I can share a one-page template of Medistry's procurement ask.

Best,
Sara
Sara Khan
Head of Procurement, Medistry Health
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara.khan@medistry.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HIPAA package pricing — evidence delivery and amortization question

Sara —

Thanks for laying this out. Below is a concise sketch you can share with finance/security; happy to turn this into a short appendix to the SOW.

High-level pricing split (proposal):
- Implementation (one-time): $65k — covers HSM key bootstrap, residency cutover support, and one-time audit evidence package. Capitalizable.
- Recurring (monthly): $8k/month — audit log retention tier + KMS seat licensing (covers operational KMS usage at 2 seats).
- Optional extras: Additional HSM seats at $1,200/seat/month; extended audit retention beyond 12 months billed at $0.02/GB/month.

Proposed concessions for 12-month reserved commit: 18% off recurring fees + full waiver of first-month recurring for pilot (applied as credit). Implementation fee can be amortized into a 12-month payment plan on the invoice if you prefer CAPEX smoothing.

Evidence delivery (what Redwood will provide):
- Delivery cadence: initial package within 10 business days of pilot start; quarterly exports thereafter on request.
- Format: ZIP containing CSV audit log extracts, signed attestation of retention window, and a short operational runbook (PDF).
- We maintain an internal checklist for evidence handoff — attaching the Audit_Evidence_Checklist.xlsx for your security team's review.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Ben and I finalize a short pricing appendix matching the SOW language and return a redline.
2) You confirm whether Medistry needs a capitalizable invoice schedule or prefers a single up-front implementation charge.
3) If the security team wants any specific log fields or parity with a SOC-2 schema, enumerate those and we'll include them in the quarterly export template.

Assigning Ben to help with discount tiers and Laura to draft the SOW appendix.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales, Compliance Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara.khan@medistry.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HIPAA package pricing — evidence delivery and amortization question

Quick note from pricing: Hannah's sketch is the right starting point. Couple of clarifications and an alternate path that often makes Medistry-style finance teams happiest.

Alternate (blended) charge approach:
- Implementation: reduce to $45k if Medistry commits to 24 months reserved capacity (we amortize remaining $20k as a pre-paid credit over months 13–24).
- Recurring: same base $8k/month; for commit above 2M tokens/month we can tier down to $6.8k/month after hitting the volume threshold.
- KMS seat accounting: we can present the KMS fee either as a separate monthly line (for operational transparency) or as a passed-through license that we include in the recurring blended price. If your auditors prefer line-items, choose the separate approach.

Attachments: dropping an early SOW draft into the thread (Medistry_SOW_v1.pdf) — contains a draft clause for \"Evidence Delivery & Audit Support\" that reads: "Redwood will provide an initial audit evidence package within 10 business days of pilot activation and quarterly exports thereafter upon request. Redwood will maintain retention for 12 months by default; extended retention is available at an agreed rate."

If Medistry confirms a preference on the invoice presentation (single capitalizable implementation invoice vs. small up-front + amortized credit), we'll produce both sample invoice options for CFO review.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Khan <sara.khan@medistry.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonathan Park <jonathan.park@medistry.com>
Date: 2026-12-22T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HIPAA package pricing — evidence delivery and amortization question

Thanks Hannah/Ben — this is helpful and close to what procurement needs. A few follow-ups:

1) Our CFO prefers the blended charge (reduce implementation up-front, amortize remainder across months 13–24). Please send sample invoices that show the amortization schedule.
2) We do need the audit exports to include columns X-EventID, X-UserID, ResourcePath, ActionType, and a hashed UID for PHI correlation — can you confirm those fields are available? If not, we'll need the log schema.
3) On discounts: the 18% is acceptable for a 12-months pilot. If we agree to a 24-month commit, can you confirm the blended implementation reduction Ben described and whether the discount increases to 22%?

Also, our legal team will want a short contract clause specifying that evidence deliveries are not considered "production support" and will be delivered on a best-effort quarterly cadence unless a separate support SLAs are purchased.

If you can provide the sample invoices + a redlined SOW appendix, we can aim to circulate to legal on Thursday.

Regards,
Sara
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara.khan@medistry.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-22T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HIPAA package pricing — evidence delivery and amortization question

Sara — great, thanks. Quick confirmations and next steps below.

Confirmations:
- We can include the requested fields in the CSV exports (X-EventID, X-UserID, ResourcePath, ActionType, hashed UID). Laura will attach a sample schema snippet in the redline.
- For 24-month commit: implementation up-front reduced to $45k (as Ben proposed) and discount on recurring increases to 22%. We'll show both the 12- and 24-month pricing tables in the invoice examples.
- Evidence clause: below is a concise draft you can hand to legal — feel free to redline.

DRAFT CLAUSE (for SOW appendix):
"Evidence Delivery & Audit Support: Redwood will deliver an initial Audit Evidence Package within ten (10) business days following Pilot Activation. Thereafter, Redwood will provide Audit Log Exports on a quarterly basis upon Customer request. Audit Log Exports will include the fields identified in Appendix A. Audit deliveries are provided as part of the HIPAA add-on; ongoing operational support for troubleshooting or investigative analysis is not included and requires a separate support agreement with defined SLAs."

Action items (owners):
- Laura: produce 2 sample invoice PDFs (12-month and 24-month amortization schedules) and attach to the HubSpot deal. HubSpot ref HS-4521. (Due: 2026-12-23 EOD)
- Marissa: add the sample log schema and redline SOW appendix (attach Medistry_SOW_v1.pdf with edits). (Due: 2026-12-23 EOD)
- Ben: prepare the discount confirmation and final pricing table. (Due: 2026-12-23 morning)
- Sara/Jonathan: confirm legal's preference on the "best-effort" vs. "SLA-backed" language.

I'll follow up with the attachments in the morning. Thanks for the quick turnaround — looking forward to closing this pilot.

Best,
Hannah
